title: Goal Parser Interpretation
statement:
A goal parser reads a command string made only of the tokens `G`, `()` and `(al)`, written one after another in any order. It translates each token and joins the results in the original order:

- `G` becomes `G`
- `()` becomes `o`
- `(al)` becomes `al`

Given the command string, print what the parser produces.
input_format: A single line containing the command string.
constraints: command is a concatenation of the tokens `G`, `()` and `(al)`

examples.explanation: G stays G, () becomes o and (al) becomes al, giving Goal.
The tokens are (al), (al), G and (), which translate to al, al, G and o.
Three empty-bracket tokens, each translated to o.

hints: Walk through the string from left to right with an index; the character under the index tells you which token starts there.
If it is `G`, emit `G`. If it is `(`, look at the next character: `)` means the token is `()`, otherwise it is `(al)`.
Advance the index by the length of the token you just consumed (1, 2 or 4).
reference:
import sys

def main():
    s = sys.stdin.read().strip()
    out = []
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        if s[i] == 'G':
            out.append('G')
            i += 1
        elif s[i + 1] == ')':
            out.append('o')
            i += 2
        else:
            out.append('al')
            i += 4
    print(''.join(out))

main()

    tests.append(''.join(parts))
